results.name: Pull Up Normal Grip
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles and pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
results.description: Pull Up Normal Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View)
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles to pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
results.description: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull
instructions: Sit tall on the machine chair, or a cable seat, and take the overhead handles with your arms extended.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Pull the handles down toward your shoulders by driving your elbows down and back.
Return the handles overhead with control and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid leaning back to finish the rep.
results.description: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Rear Shoulders.

results.name: Resistance Band - Cable Row
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Kneel on one knee with the opposite leg forward, foot flat on the ground.
Hold the band handles with both hands, arms extended forward, and palms facing down.
Pull the band handles towards your chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the row to maximize back activation.
Adjust the resistance band tension or your kneeling position for an appropriate challenge.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; keep them down and relaxed.
results.description: Resistance Band - Cable Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
results.description: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with a loop resistance band over your ankles and another loop resistance band over your forearms. Extend your arms forward and keep your legs straight.
Engage your core and glutes, and lift your chest and legs off the floor simultaneously, spreading your legs apart against the resistance of the band.
Squeeze your lower back muscles at the top of the movement, keeping your arms and legs straight.
Slowly lower your chest and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Focus on engaging your lower back and glute muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your chest and legs and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders.

results.name: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Kneel on the floor on your right knee and your left foot flat on the floor, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
results.description: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms crossed under your head, resting your forehead on your arms. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your legs extended and feet together.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your legs straight off the floor while keeping your head resting on your arms.
While lifting your legs, open them wide apart against the band's resistance, keeping your legs straight.
Slowly bring your legs back together while lowering your legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift and open your legs, and inhale as you bring them back together and lower them.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and protect your lower back.
results.description: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) at shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended above you.
Engage your core and keep your back straight. Lean back slightly to create a natural arch in your lower back.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, bringing your elbows down to your sides while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the weight.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid letting them bend backward.
results.description: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet secure on the foot platform. Grasp the V bar with both hands.
Sit upright with your back straight, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Pull the V bar towards your abdomen by bringing your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight throughout the exercise to avoid strain.
Engage your core to maintain stability and proper posture.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.
